title: OBT: 3 Biggest Broncos Changes for Camp — Waddle’s Arrival, Webb’s Offense & a New D‑Line Reality
text: It’s a solo Monday edition of Orange & Blue Today , and Cecil Lammey breaks down the 3 BIGGEST CHANGES for the Broncos as training camp opens — the shifts that define how different this team looks from the last time we saw them in the AFC Championship Game. The unfinished business from that loss — and the clear need for an offensive upgrade — led Denver to make a franchise‑shaking move: Trading for Jaylen Waddle . Waddle’s arrival instantly changes spacing, explosiveness, and how defenses must play the Broncos. Cecil explains why this move wasn’t just about adding talent — it was about raising the ceiling of the entire offense. Next, the biggest philosophical shift: Davis Webb takes over full‑time play‑calling duties from Sean Payton. What does Webb bring. How does the offense evolve. And why could this change make the Broncos better and more adaptable in 2026. Cecil breaks down the scheme tweaks, rhythm changes, and QB‑friendly elements Webb is expected to emphasize. And finally, the trenches: With John Franklin‑Meyers gone, the Broncos defensive line enters camp with new faces, new roles, and a new identity. Cecil dives into who steps up, how the rotation shifts, and what the front looks like without one of its most reliable disruptors. These aren’t small tweaks — they’re foundational changes that reshape the Broncos’ path toward finishing the job they left on the table last January. 🔥 In this episode: Why Waddle’s arrival transforms the offense instantly How Davis Webb’s play‑calling changes the Broncos’ identity What the defensive line looks like without Franklin‑Meyers Why these three changes matter most as camp opens Drop your take — which change impacts the Broncos the most as they chase unfinished business in 2026.
